target_customer: Medicare and Medicare Advantage seniors with chronic illness, billed through insurers
problem: Loneliness and isolation lower medication adherence and worsen outcomes for seniors with chronic conditions.
business_model: In-network telehealth provider billing Medicare for collaborative care and group programs
product_category: Telehealth, behavioral health and collaborative care management

founders.name: Rahul Sharma
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; Crunchbase aggregator lists him as CEO. No background found.

founders.name: Naina Limbekar
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Telehealth scheduling and group sessions use standard tools; the harder part is clinical and billing compliance.

defensibility.rationale: In-network payer contracts and licensed provider operations take time, but the model can be copied by other telehealth providers.

market_need_then: The YC page cites one in two Americans with a chronic condition, 50 percent medication adherence, and over 1 trillion dollars in direct costs.

brand_strength.rationale: Only directory listings and one undated press release about a 360 degree therapy program were found; no brand specific coverage.

outcome_analysis: Little public information exists for Reviving Mind beyond the YC listing and directory profiles. It is described as active, scaling in the US, and offering collaborative care management, with no funding, exit or distress reported. Unknown funding is not zero, so no outcome can be assigned and no success or failure factors are supported by sources.
notes: The company website returned HTTP 503 when fetched, not confirmed dead. Competitor list empty: searches found no dated source naming rivals. Aggregators conflict on HQ (Boston vs San Francisco) and leadership; Dealroom enterprise value 500k to 750k is not tied to a round. An undated PRWeb release announces a 360 degree therapy program.
